mainTopic: Public חילול שבת and מומר status, and the משנה on giving and renouncing courtyard רשות for עירוב חצרות
overview: The amud opens with the end of a challenge to רב הונא, who said that a Jew who publicly desecrates שבת is a מומר. The challenge is a ברייתא saying that only עבודה זרה makes someone a מומר for the whole תורה. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רב הונא meant only that such a person cannot give or renounce רשות in a courtyard. He supports this with a ברייתא contrasting how a Jew and a גוי transfer rights. רב אשי answers that רב הונא's rule is general and follows a תנא who equates שבת with עבודה זרה. He proves it from a ברייתא about accepting קרבנות from sinners, which lists the one who pours wine for idols together with the public מחלל שבת. Then a new משנה teaches what happens when one or two residents forget to join the עירוב חצרות, and who may give or receive רשות. The גמרא explains the משנה's wording: the house versus the courtyard, the idea of a guest, and why two who forgot block each other. The amud ends partway through an answer about why the rule that two may give רשות is not obvious, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The challenge ends: only idol worship makes someone a full apostate
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the ברייתא quoted against רב הונא: a person is not a מומר for the whole תורה unless he is a מומר for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...until he is an apostate for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge against רב הונא. The ברייתא it quotes says that a person becomes a מומר for the whole תורה only through עבודה זרה, so breaking שבת alone should not make him one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treated a Jew who publicly breaks שבת as a מומר. The ברייתא seems to say that breaking a single מצוה, even שבת, does not give a person that status. Only עבודה זרה does. So רב הונא's ruling looks like it contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An apostate; a Jew who has rejected observance of the תורה
Idol worship
Until he becomes

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The first part of the challenge, which states רב הונא's view and opens the ברייתא, comes on the previous amud. This line is only the punchline of that challenge.

phrases.english: until he is an apostate with regard to idol worship.
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא used to challenge רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that a Jew who publicly desecrates שבת is a מומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits full מומר status to someone who worships עבודה זרה. Breaking שבת alone should therefore not make a person a מומר.

steps.title: רב הונא meant only giving and renouncing courtyard rights
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רב הונא never meant מומר in general. He meant only that such a person cannot give or renounce רשות in a courtyard the way a regular Jew can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is about giving rights and renouncing rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge by narrowing רב הונא's statement. רב הונא was talking only about the עירוב rules of giving up and transferring rights in a courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about being a מומר for the whole תורה. רב הונא was talking about one narrow area of הלכה. In that area, a public שבת desecrator is treated differently, but that does not make him a מומר for everything. So the two sources do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Rights or a share in a domain, such as a courtyard
To give away one's rights to another person
To renounce one's rights in a domain

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
[Rav Huna meant only] for giving rights and renouncing rights.
phrases.notes: This limits רב הונא's ruling to the laws of עירובין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לִיתֵּן רְשׁוּת וּלְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא meant that a public שבת desecrator is a מומר for the whole תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא meant only that such a person cannot give or renounce courtyard rights like a regular Jew

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the narrow reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a מומר who keeps שבת in public can renounce רשות. One who does not keep שבת in public cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as it was taught: An apostate Jew who keeps his Shabbat in the marketplace can renounce rights. One who does not keep his Shabbat in the marketplace cannot renounce rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב נחמן בר יצחק. It links public שבת observance directly to the ability to renounce רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the person's public שבת behavior to one specific law, renouncing courtyard rights. That is exactly the narrow scope רב נחמן בר יצחק described. If he keeps שבת publicly, he is treated as a Jew for this purpose. If he does not, he is treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And as it was taught in a ברייתא; introduces support
Keeps his שבת
In the marketplace, meaning in public
He can renounce his rights

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "keeps his שבת in the marketplace" refers to his public behavior. The ברייתא cares about what he does openly, not what he does privately.

phrases.english: And as it was taught: An apostate Jew,
[if he] keeps his Shabbat in the marketplace, he can renounce rights;
[if he] does not keep his Shabbat in the marketplace,
he cannot renounce rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source supporting the answer in step 2
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that public שבת desecration matters for ביטול רשות

steps.title: Why it matters: a Jew transfers rights by speech, a גוי only by renting
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains its rule. A Jew can take or give רשות with just a statement, but a גוי's rights can be handled only by renting them out. It also gives the exact words a Jew uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they said: A Jew can take rights and give rights, but with a gentile, only once he rents [it out]. How? He says to him: My rights are acquired by you, my rights are renounced to you. He acquires, and there is no need to take formal possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains why public שבת observance matters here. A Jew can hand over rights with words alone, while a גוי needs an actual rental.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מומר who does not keep שבת publicly is treated like a גוי for these rules. So his rights cannot be cancelled with a simple statement. A regular Jew just says "My rights are acquired by you" or "My rights are renounced to you," and that works without any formal act of קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the חכמים said; introduces the reason
Only once he rents it out
My rights are acquired by you
My rights are renounced to you
To take formal possession through a קנין

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew can give or renounce רשות by speech alone. A גוי's rights, and those of a מומר who publicly breaks שבת, can be handled only by renting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a courtyard becomes permitted for carrying on שבת. It also shows why the status of each resident matters in practice.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹטֵל רְשׁוּת וְנוֹתֵן רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: Because they said: A Jew can take rights and give rights,
but with a gentile, [not] until he rents [it out].
phrases.notes: A גוי's rights cannot simply be renounced. They must be rented.

phrases.english: How so? He says to him:
"My rights are acquired by you,"
"My rights are renounced to you" —
he acquires, and there is no need to take formal possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and explains the reason behind its rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew transfers or renounces רשות by speech alone, with no קנין needed. A גוי's rights require renting.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב הונא follows a תנא who treats שבת like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. רב הונא did mean מומר in general, and he follows a תנא who holds that breaking שבת is as severe as עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is this tanna, for whom Shabbat is as severe as idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second, different answer to the challenge. He says רב הונא follows a different תנא than the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not narrow רב הונא's statement. Instead, he says there is a תנא who treats public שבת desecration exactly like עבודה זרה. By that view, such a person is a מומר for the whole תורה. The challenging ברייתא simply follows a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: This תנא, the particular sage of the משנה period
For whom it is severe
Like idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רב נחמן בר יצחק says רב הונא's ruling covers only courtyard rights. רב אשי says it is a general ruling that follows the תנא who equates שבת with עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is [according to] this tanna
for whom Shabbat is as severe as idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the challenge in step 1, different from רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the statement to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that only עבודה זרה makes a person a מומר for the whole תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים equate public שבת desecration with עבודה זרה, and רב הונא follows them

steps.title: The ברייתא on the word "of you": some of you, not all of you
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's source begins. The word מכם in the פסוק about קרבנות excludes the מומר, and it shows that this distinction applies only to Jews, not to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Of you" means some of you, not all of you, which leaves out the מומר. "Of you" also means: among you I made a distinction, but not among the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that contains the תנא רב אשי was talking about. This first part reads the word "מכם" in the פסוק about bringing קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "מכם" ("of you") suggests that only part of כלל ישראל may bring a קרבן, so a מומר is left out. The same word also teaches that this screening applies only to Jews. A גוי's קרבן is accepted even if he does not keep his own מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
"Of you" (ויקרא א:ב), meaning some of you
Excluding the apostate
Among you I made a distinction
The nations (non-Jews)

steps.confusionAlert: "ולא באומות" does not mean that גוים cannot bring קרבנות. It means the opposite: among גוים‎, ה׳ does not separate good from bad, so any גוי's voluntary קרבן is accepted.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"Of you" — but not all of you,
phrases.notes: From ויקרא א:ב, about bringing a קרבן.

phrases.english: excluding the apostate.
"Of you" — among you I made a distinction,
but not among the nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that contains the תנא רב אשי referred to in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that a תנא treats public חילול שבת as severely as עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא expounding "מכם" and "מן הבהמה" (ויקרא א:ב)

steps.title: Sacrifices are accepted from sinners, except three types
steps.stepSummary: "מן הבהמה" includes people who act like animals. So קרבנות are accepted from Jewish sinners to help them do תשובה, except from the מומר, the one who pours wine for עבודה זרה, and the public מחלל שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Of the animals" comes to include people who behave like animals. From here the חכמים said: we accept קרבנות from Jewish sinners, so that they will come back in תשובה. This does not apply to the מומר, the one who pours wine for idols, or the one who breaks שבת in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and teaches that even sinners may bring קרבנות, with three exceptions. This list is the actual proof for רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the public מחלל שבת in the same list as the מנסך יין, who serves עבודה זרה. That shows this תנא treats public חילול שבת as being as severe as עבודה זרה, which is exactly רב אשי's point. The reason for accepting קרבנות from ordinary sinners is to draw them back toward תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: "Of the animals" (from the same פסוק)
Jewish sinners
So that they will return in repentance
One who pours wine as an offering to עבודה זרה
In public

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the public מחלל שבת is listed next to the one who pours wine for idols, this ברייתא supports רב אשי's reading of רב הונא.

phrases.english: "Of the animals" —
to include people who are like animals.
From here they said:
We accept sacrifices from Jewish sinners,
so that they will return in repentance.
Except for the apostate,
and one who pours wine (for idolatry),
and one who desecrates Shabbos in public.
phrases.notes: This line is the heart of רב אשי's proof: public חילול שבת is listed with עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that a תנא equates public חילול שבת with עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The list of exceptions: the מומר, the מנסך יין, and the public מחלל שבת

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא first excludes the מומר from bringing קרבנות, then says קרבנות are accepted from Jewish sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said "of you" and not all of you, to leave out the מומר. Then it teaches that we accept קרבנות from Jewish sinners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the ברייתא itself. One line rejects the מומר, and another line accepts sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מומר is a kind of sinner. So how can the ברייתא both reject the מומר's קרבן and accept קרבנות from פושעי ישראל? The two clauses seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)
And then it teaches
To exclude

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said "of you" but not all of you,
to exclude the apostate.
And then it teaches:
We accept sacrifices from Jewish sinners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא quoted in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's first clause (the מומר is excluded) against its middle clause (sinners are accepted)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מומר is a sinner. Rejecting the מומר while accepting sinners looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: Two kinds of מומר: for the whole תורה or for one sin
steps.stepSummary: The first clause is about a מומר for the whole תורה. The middle clause is about someone who is a מומר for only one sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The first clause is about a מומר for the entire תורה. The middle clause is about a מומר for one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each clause is talking about a different kind of מומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who has thrown off the whole תורה cannot bring a קרבן. Someone who rebels in only one area still counts as one of the פושעי ישראל, and his קרבן is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
The first clause
The middle clause
An apostate regarding the entire תורה
An apostate regarding one matter

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
the first clause is about an apostate for the entire Torah,
the middle clause is about an apostate for one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each clause refers to a different type of מומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to be about the same kind of sinner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The excluded מומר rejects the whole תורה. The accepted sinner, even a מומר, rebels in only one area.

steps.title: The last clause does not fit either kind of מומר
steps.stepSummary: The last clause excludes "the מומר." If he is a מומר for the whole תורה, this repeats the first clause. If he is a מומר for one sin, it contradicts the middle clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last clause: "except the מומר and the one who pours wine." What kind of מומר is this? If he is a מומר for the whole תורה, that is the same as the first clause. If he is a מומר for one thing, then the middle clause is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer from step 9 against the last clause of the ברייתא and finds that it does not fit either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 created only two kinds of מומר, and the מומר in the last clause must be one of them. A מומר for the whole תורה would be a pointless repetition of the first clause. A מומר for one sin would contradict the middle clause, which accepts קרבנות from such people.

keyTerms.meaning: Now say (look at) the last clause
What is the case? What does it look like?
That is the same as the first clause

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the clauses. The רישא is the first exclusion of the מומר ("מכם"). The מציעתא is "we accept from sinners." The סיפא is the list of exceptions ("חוץ מן המומר").

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
Except for the apostate and one who pours wine.
This apostate, what is the case?
If he is an apostate for the entire Torah —
that is the same as the first clause.
If he is an apostate for one matter,
the middle clause is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 9 by applying it to the last clause of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from step 9 (the first clause means a מומר for the whole תורה, the middle clause a מומר for one sin)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מומר in the last clause must be one of the two types. One option makes the clause a repetition, and the other makes it contradict the middle clause.

steps.title: The last clause means pouring wine for idols and public חילול שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the last clause. 'Except the מומר' means except the one who pours wine for עבודה זרה and the one who desecrates שבת in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it means: 'except the מומר to pour wine for idols and to desecrate שבת in public'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 10. The last clause does not describe a new, separate kind of מומר. It explains which two sins are so severe that they count as rejecting the whole תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the last clause either repeats the first clause or contradicts the middle clause. The answer is that the last clause defines the first clause. Two specific sins, pouring wine for idols and public חילול שבת, put a person in the same category as a מומר for the whole תורה, even though each is only one sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this what it is saying (introduces a rereading of a text)
to pour wine as an offering to עבודה זרה
in public

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'pours wine' and 'desecrates שבת' as just two more examples of a one-sin מומר. The point is that these two sins are so severe that they count like a מומר for the whole תורה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:
Apart from the apostate with regard to pouring wine libations to idols
phrases.notes: The word מומר connects to both actions that follow.

phrases.english: and desecrating Shabbat in public?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the either-way problem raised against the last clause in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the clause: it defines which one-sin sinners count as a full מומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The מומר' in the last clause looked like either a repetition or a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last clause names two sins, wine for idols and public חילול שבת, that make a person count like a מומר for the whole תורה.

steps.title: עבודה זרה and public חילול שבת are equal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists עבודה זרה and public חילול שבת side by side, so the two are equally severe. The proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that עבודה זרה and שבת are equal to each other. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the reading in step 11. There is a תנא who treats public חילול שבת exactly like עבודה זרה, and the גמרא accepts this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both sins appear together in one exception, the ברייתא puts them on the same level. This gives רב אשי the source he wanted. 'שמע מינה' tells us the proof is accepted and this part of the סוגיא is closed.

keyTerms.meaning: So it is evident; this shows
they are like each other; they are equal
learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew who publicly desecrates שבת is treated like one who worships idols. His קרבנות are not accepted, even though for other single sins we do accept קרבנות to help a sinner do תשובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This equation is what lets רב אשי read רב הונא's statement as a general rule. According to the תנא of this ברייתא, a public מחלל שבת is a מומר for the whole תורה, just like one who serves עבודה זרה, and not only for ביטול רשות as רב נחמן בר יצחק explained.

phrases.english: It is apparent that idolatry and Shabbat
are equivalent to one another.
Learn from this that it is so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשַׁבָּת כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final inference from the rereading in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תנא treats public חילול שבת as equal in severity to עבודה זרה, and the גמרא accepts this as proven.

steps.title: One resident forgot to join the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If one resident forgot to join the עירוב and gave up his rights, no one may carry between his house and the courtyard, but everyone may carry from the other houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Residents of a courtyard where one of them forgot and did not join the עירוב: his house is forbidden for bringing things in and taking things out, both for him and for them. But their houses are permitted, both for him and for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a basic case. One neighbor forgot the עירוב and has given up his rights in the courtyard to the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he gives up his rights, the courtyard belongs only to the others, so they may carry between their houses and the courtyard. Even he may carry from their houses, since he is now like a guest in their courtyard. But his own house is still his separate domain, so no one may carry between his house and the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (the opening of the משנה section)
residents who share a courtyard
joined the עירוב חצרות
to carry in and to carry out

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say it openly, but this case assumes the forgetful neighbor has already given up his rights (ביטול רשות). Without that, the whole courtyard would be forbidden to everyone.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Residents of a courtyard, one of whom forgot
and did not participate in the eiruv —
his house is prohibited for bringing in or taking out
phrases.notes: Carrying between his house and the courtyard.

phrases.english: both to him and to them,
but their houses are permitted both to him and to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכַח אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְלֹא עֵירַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the forgetful resident gives up his rights, his own house is closed off for carrying, while the other houses are open for carrying for everyone.

steps.title: If the others give their rights to him
steps.stepSummary: If instead the others give up their rights to the one who forgot, he may carry and they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they gave him their rights, he is permitted and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns the case around. Now the majority hands the courtyard over to the one who forgot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard now belongs only to him, so he may carry between his house and the courtyard. The others, who gave up their rights, may not carry from their own houses into it. Giving up rights works in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: rights or ownership in a domain (here, in the courtyard)
they gave him their rights; they renounced their rights in his favor

phrases.english: If they gave away their rights to him —
he is permitted, and they are prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse case of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever receives everyone's rights may carry. Those who gave their rights away may not.

steps.title: Two who forgot block each other
steps.stepSummary: If two residents forgot, giving rights to them does not help, because they forbid each other. One person can give and receive rights, but two can only give.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two, they forbid each other. For one person can give rights and receive rights, but two can give rights and cannot receive rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where two people forgot the עירוב. It explains why the others cannot hand the courtyard over to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard went to both of them, it would be shared by two people with separate houses and no עירוב between them. So each would forbid the other from carrying. That is why two people can give up rights but cannot usefully receive them.

keyTerms.meaning: they forbid carrying to each other
gives up rights
receives rights

phrases.english: If there were two who forgot —
they prohibit one another.
For one may give away rights and receive rights,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם נוֹתְנִין רְשׁוּת וְאֵין נוֹטְלִין רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: two may give away rights but may not receive rights.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹסְרִין זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 14 from one forgetful resident to two, and states the general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rights can be given to one person but not to two who have no עירוב together, because they forbid each other.

steps.title: When may rights be given up
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks when one may give up rights. בית שמאי say only before שבת begins; בית הלל say even after dark, on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when may one give up rights? בית שמאי say: while it is still day. בית הלל say: after it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a timing question and records a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that giving up rights is like a transfer of ownership, so it must be done before שבת. בית הלל allow it even on שבת, so a person who forgot the עירוב can still fix the problem after שבת has begun.

keyTerms.meaning: from when
while it is still day, before שבת
after dark, once שבת has begun

phrases.english: When may one give away rights?
Beit Shammai say: While it is still day.
Beit Hillel say: Even after nightfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who may receive rights to when rights may be given up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: בית שמאי allow giving up rights only before שבת; בית הלל allow it even after dark.

steps.title: Carrying after giving up rights
steps.stepSummary: If someone gave up his rights and then carried into the courtyard, רבי מאיר says he makes it forbidden either way. רבי יהודה says only if he did it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who gave up his rights and then carried out, whether by mistake or on purpose, makes it forbidden; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: on purpose, he makes it forbidden; by mistake, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dispute about someone whose actions go against the rights he gave away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By carrying, he acts as if the courtyard is still his, which seems to take back his ביטול רשות. רבי מאיר says any such act cancels it, even one done by mistake. רבי יהודה says only a deliberate act counts as taking it back; a mistake is just forgetting.

keyTerms.meaning: by mistake; unknowingly
on purpose; deliberately
makes carrying forbidden for everyone

steps.whatToRemember: Main points of the משנה: rights can be given to one person but not to two; בית הלל allow giving up rights even on שבת; and רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about whether a mistaken act of carrying cancels the gift of rights.

phrases.english: One who gave away his rights and then carried out,
whether unwittingly or intentionally —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: he renders it prohibited; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Intentionally, he renders it prohibited; unwittingly, he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the timing question, addresses whether a later act can cancel a gift of rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: רבי מאיר says carrying cancels the gift of rights even by mistake; רבי יהודה says only when done on purpose.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: only his house is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that only the forgetful resident's house is forbidden, while his share of the courtyard is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: It is his house that is forbidden. This implies that his courtyard is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by drawing an inference from the exact wording of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said carrying between his house and the courtyard is forbidden. The גמרא concludes that the problem is his house only. His part of the courtyard is open for the others to use.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
His house
His courtyard (his share of it)
Is permitted

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is his house that is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading the משנה's wording closely: it says only his house is forbidden.

phrases.english: which implies that his courtyard is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּיתוֹ הוּא דְּאָסוּר, הָא חֲצֵירוֹ שַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the wording, only the forgetful resident's house is forbidden. His courtyard share is permitted.

steps.title: Either way, the split makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference. If he gave up his rights, why is his house forbidden? If he did not, why is his courtyard permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he gave up his rights, why is his house forbidden? If he did not give up his rights, why is his courtyard permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference with a two-sided question, a dilemma. Neither option seems to explain why the house and the courtyard are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he gave up his rights, he should not forbid anything, not even his house. If he did not, he should forbid everything, even the courtyard. Treating them differently seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Gave up (renounced) his rights
Why?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he renounced, why is his house forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא בַּטֵּיל, חֲצֵירוֹ אַמַּאי שַׁרְיָא?
phrases.english: If he did not renounce, why is his courtyard permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The split ruling: his house is forbidden, but his courtyard is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Giving up rights is all-or-nothing, so either both areas should be permitted or both forbidden.

steps.title: He gave up the courtyard but not the house
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he gave up his rights in the courtyard but kept his rights in his house. The רבנן hold that giving up the courtyard does not include the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where he gave up his rights in the courtyard but not in his house. The רבנן hold that one who gives up his courtyard rights has not given up his house rights, because a person can live in a house without a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dilemma. The resident gave up only part of his rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up rights is not all-or-nothing. The house and the courtyard can be separated. Since a house can be lived in without a courtyard, giving up the courtyard does not automatically include the house.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (introduces a specific case)
Rights or ownership claim to an area
The Sages (majority opinion)
Lives, dwells

steps.whatToRemember: Giving up rights in the courtyard is not giving up rights in the house. A person can live in a house without a courtyard.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Such as where he renounced his rights in his courtyard,
but did not renounce his rights in his house.
And the Rabbis hold:
One who renounces his rights in his courtyard
has not renounced his rights in his house,
because a person lives in a house without a courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving up rights covers everything at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gave up only the courtyard. According to the רבנן, the house stays his because a house can stand on its own.

steps.title: Why may he use the others' houses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה allows the forgetful resident, as well as the others, to carry in the others' houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And carrying in their houses is permitted for him and for them. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forgetful resident never joined the עירוב. So it is surprising that he may carry in and out of their houses.

keyTerms.meaning: Theirs (their houses)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And theirs is permitted to him and to them,
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the forgetful resident may carry in the others' houses.

steps.title: He is like their guest
steps.stepSummary: He counts as a guest of the other residents, so he may carry wherever they may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he is like a guest with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the forgetful resident is treated like a guest staying with the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guest does not create his own rights in a place. He follows his hosts. Since they gave up nothing and are permitted, he is permitted along with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Guest
In relation to them, with them

phrases.english: Because he is a guest in relation to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is a guest among them and follows their permission.

steps.title: Why can't they be his guests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case where the others gave him their rights, and asks why they cannot then be treated as his guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they gave him their rights, he is permitted and they are forbidden. But let them be like guests with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the 'guest' idea from the last step to challenge another ruling of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one person can be a guest of the many, why can't the many be guests of the one? Then they too should be permitted to carry, yet the משנה forbids them.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave him their rights
But let them be (a challenging suggestion)
Guests (plural)

phrases.english: If they gave him their rights,
he is permitted and they are forbidden.
But let them be like guests with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the guest reasoning of step 22 to the ruling of step 14 and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the others are forbidden after giving him their rights.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If guest status works one way, it should work the other way too.

steps.title: One among many is a guest, many with one are not
steps.stepSummary: One person among five counts as a guest, but five people with one person do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One in relation to five is a guest. Five in relation to one are not guests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that guest status only goes one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single person living among a group naturally fits in as their guest. A whole group is not seen as the guests of one person. So the many stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One in relation to five
Is not considered

steps.whatToRemember: Guest status works for one person among many, not for many people with one.
steps.confusionAlert: The number five is just an example of 'many.' The point is a group versus an individual, not that exact number.

phrases.english: One in relation to five is a guest;

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה לְגַבֵּי חַד — לָא הָוֵי אוֹרֵחַ.
phrases.english: five in relation to one are not a guest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Guest status works in both directions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an individual among a group counts as a guest. A group with an individual does not.

steps.title: Trying to prove that people can renounce back and forth
steps.stepSummary: From the order of the משנה, the גמרא suggests a proof that rights can be renounced and then renounced back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: people may renounce their rights, and then renounce again in the other direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the order of the משנה's cases. It suggests that this order proves a new rule: after one person gives up his rights, the others can later give their rights back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first says the forgetful resident gave up his rights to the others. It then says the others gave their rights to him. Read as one continuous story, that would mean ביטול רשות can go one way and then be reversed the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a proof formula)
They renounce / give up their rights
And then renounce again (in the other direction)

phrases.english: Learn from this:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to suggest something we can learn from the משנה.

phrases.english: they may renounce, and then renounce back again.
phrases.notes: First the forgetful one renounces to them, then they renounce to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the 'guest' discussion, the גמרא draws a new inference from the order of the משנה's clauses.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ביטול רשות can be done back and forth (מבטלין וחוזרין ומבטלין).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the משנה: first he renounces to them, then they renounce to him.

steps.title: No proof: the second case is a separate situation
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's clause about the others giving him their rights describes a separate case where they gave from the start, not a reversal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: if they gave him their rights from the outset, he is permitted and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The second clause is not a continuation of the first story. It is a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the case where the others give him their rights stands on its own, the משנה never describes renouncing and then renouncing back. So nothing can be learned from it about back-and-forth ביטול רשות.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (re-reading the text)
From the outset / at the beginning
Their rights (in the חצר)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say back-and-forth renouncing is forbidden here. It only says this משנה cannot prove it.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
if they gave him their rights at the outset —
phrases.notes: A separate case, not after he renounced to them.

phrases.english: he is permitted and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 25 by re-reading the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not rule on whether back-and-forth renouncing works.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the clauses are one continuous story. In fact the second clause is an independent case where they gave 'from the outset'.

steps.title: Why say that two forgetful residents restrict each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about two who forgot an עירוב and asks why it needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if there were two, they forbid each other. But isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about two people who forgot to make an עירוב. It asks why the משנה bothered to teach something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the others give their rights to two people who have no עירוב between them, those two still share the חצר without an עירוב. Of course they restrict each other. So the line seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbid (carrying) for each other
It is obvious! (challenge: why teach it?)

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹסְרִין זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: If there were two, they forbid one another.
Isn't that obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line 'היו שנים אוסרין זה על זה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two people without an עירוב obviously restrict each other, so the line seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The new case: one of the two renounced to the other
steps.stepSummary: The line teaches that even if one of the two later renounced to the other, it does not help, since he had no permission in the חצר when he renounced.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where one of them then gave up his rights to his friend. You might have said the friend is now permitted. So the משנה teaches us that since, at the time he renounced, he had no permission in this חצר, it does not help.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line covers a less obvious case. After the others renounce to the two, one of the two renounces to the other. The משנה teaches that they still restrict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the second person should now be alone and permitted. But when the renunciation happened, neither of the two was allowed to carry in that חצר. A renunciation made while he had no permission there does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a special case)
You might have said
It teaches us (the new point)
Permission (to carry)
At the time

steps.whatToRemember: A ביטול רשות made when the person had no permission in the חצר does not take effect. So the two still forbid each other.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where one of them then went back
and renounced his rights to his fellow.
You might have said: let it be permitted.
So it teaches us
that since at the time that he renounced
he did not have permission
in this courtyard.
phrases.notes: So the renunciation does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by placing the line in a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the line refers to a later renunciation between the two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once one of the two renounces to the other, the other should be alone and permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The renunciation fails, because at that time the renouncer had no permission in the חצר. They still forbid each other.

steps.title: Why add 'one person gives rights'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה adds an explanation about one giving rights, since giving and receiving were both already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה explains: for one person gives rights. Why do I need this too? If it means giving, we already learned it. If it means receiving, we already learned that too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's explanatory line 'שאחד נותן רשות' and asks why it is needed. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier clauses already showed that a single person can give up rights (the forgetful one renounced to the others). They also showed that a single person can receive rights (the others renounced to him). So repeating it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives (away) rights
Takes / receives (rights)
Why do I need this further?

phrases.english: For one gives rights.
Why do I need this further?
If it is about giving — we already learned it;
if it is about receiving — we already learned it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and challenges whether it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's explanatory line 'שאחד נותן רשות'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both giving and receiving rights by one person were already taught in earlier clauses, so the line looks redundant.

steps.title: The wording was needed for the latter clause: two can give rights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 29: the משנה needed its wording because of the latter clause, which teaches that two people can give away their רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter clause is what the משנה needed: that two people can give away their rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 29. The extra wording is there because of the סיפא, the end of the line, which teaches that even two people can give away their rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 asked why the משנה spells out giving rights, since giving and receiving were already taught. The answer is that the new idea is in the latter clause. It teaches that giving rights is not limited to one person, because two people can also give theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or ending part of a משנה
He (the תנא) needed it; it was necessary to teach
Two people may give away their rights in the חצר

phrases.english: He needed it for the latter clause:
phrases.notes: The answer points to the end of the משנה's line.

phrases.english: two may give away rights.
phrases.notes: This is the new teaching found in the latter clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocates the novelty (חידוש) to the latter clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording looked repetitive, since giving and receiving were already taught.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line exists to teach that two people may give rights.

steps.title: But two giving rights is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule that two can give away their rights is itself obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 30. If one person can give away his rights, then two people can surely do the same, so why teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving away rights is something each resident does for himself. It seems to make no difference whether one person does it or two. So the supposed new teaching does not look new at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This too; this as well
It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: But this too is obvious!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why we need this teaching, since it seems to add nothing new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'two may give rights' is a new teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one person can give away his rights, two people can obviously do the same, so the rule is not new.

steps.title: Opening of the answer: you might have thought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with 'מהו דתימא', setting up a mistaken assumption the משנה wants to rule out. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain what mistaken idea a person could have had without this rule, and it finishes the thought on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהו דתימא' always brings a הוה אמינא, meaning a reasonable but wrong first thought. The גמרא is about to show why 'two may give rights' is not actually obvious. A person might have had a reason to think it does not work, and the משנה teaches that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken first assumption (הוה אמינא)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished here. Do not read 'מהו דתימא' as the full answer. The actual reasoning continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: lest you say:
phrases.notes: This starts a הוה אמינא, something we might have thought, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the objection of step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistaken assumption (הוה אמינא) that the משנה comes to reject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: To be spelled out on the next amud: a reason to think that two people giving rights might not work
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that two may give rights, rejecting that mistaken thought (details continue next passage).
